answer: Through the prism of market discipline, Harberger-taxed identity makes Sybil farming a losing trade: each identity self-assesses a public value V, pays a per-epoch tax r*V that is burned, and anyone may buy it at V. An attacker with N puppets pays N*r*V each epoch; the delta between declared value and real earnings is pure burn. Lowball V and rivals snap the inlet of cheap identities away; price V high and the tax bleeds the farm dry first. Unlike one-time burns the cost compounds each epoch, so parked Sybil stockpiles rot: Sybil cost stays linear in N and in time, no bulk discount.
